title.description: The hook shown big on the first slide: a surprising, complete statement.

cover.description: Optional photo behind the title on the first slide.

src.description: File name in content/media/<post-id>/, e.g. "diagram.svg", or an https:// URL on upload.wikimedia.org or thumb.wikimedia.org

body.description: The caption: 2–5 sentences explaining why or how. Supports **bold**, *italic*, [links](https://…).

slides.description: Extra carousel slides after the title slide.

lab.description: Which built-in lab to show: an experiment the reader runs themselves. shared/labs.ts lists them.

prompt.description: What to try: the goal, in one or two short sentences.

takeaway.description: What the reader has found out, shown in place of the prompt once they reach the goal.

src.description: File name in content/media/<post-id>/, e.g. "diagram.svg", or an https:// URL on upload.wikimedia.org or thumb.wikimedia.org

alt.description: What the image shows, for screen readers.

fit.description: "cover" fills the slide (photos); "contain" shows the whole image on the field colours (diagrams). Default cover.

src.description: The panel art: a 4:5 picture (1080 × 1350) with no words in it. The app letters the caption and bubbles on top.

alt.description: What the panel shows, for screen readers. The caption and bubbles are read out after it.

caption.description: The narrator's box: where and when, and the facts. Dates and numbers belong here, not in a bubble.

captionAt.description: Where the caption box sits. Default top.

bubbles.description: Speech, thought or shout bubbles, in reading order (left to right, top to bottom).

text.description: The words, lettered in capitals. Real people only say what the record says they said, wrote or did.

speaker.description: Who speaks, read out by screen readers, e.g. "John Snow".

x.description: Centre of the bubble across the panel, 0 (left edge) to 100 (right edge).

y.description: Centre of the bubble down the panel, 0 (top) to 100 (bottom).

width.description: Bubble width in percent of the panel's width. Default 46.

tail.description: Where the tail points: the speaker's mouth (or head, for a thought), in the same units. Leave it out for a voice from off the panel.

kind.description: Default "speech". "thought" is a cloud with bubbles for a tail; "shout" a jagged burst; "laugh" laughter (HA HA!) lettered with shake marks and no balloon, beside the laugher and without a tail.

timing.description: How this bubble meets the one before it. "interrupts": it cuts that line off, so the line before ends with a dash (—) and this bubble overlaps its edge, drawn on top. "together": both are said at once, so the two bubbles overlap.

credit.description: Who drew the art and its licence, if not the post's author.

value.description: The big number, e.g. "86 billion" or "3×".

text.description: A real, verifiable quotation. Never invent or misattribute quotes.

options.description: 2–4 short answers; make the wrong ones plausible.

answer.description: Index of the correct option, counting from 0.

explanation.description: Shown after answering: why that is the answer.

prompt.description: The teaser or question shown first.

detail.description: A line of context under the answer.

question.description: What to guess, e.g. "How hot is the surface of Venus?"

step.description: Slider step; defaults to a hundredth of the range.

answer.description: The real value, between min and max.

heading.description: The instruction, e.g. "Oldest first" or "Smallest to largest".

items.description: In the correct order; the app shuffles them.

explanation.description: Shown after the reader has ordered them.

heading.description: What the bars compare, e.g. "CO₂ per person, tonnes a year".

value.description: The number, in the unit the slide names.

items.description: Bars, top to bottom. Values must be 0 or more.

note.description: A line under the chart: the year, the measure, a caveat.

heading.description: The statement the icons show, e.g. "1 in 4 adults don’t get enough exercise".

icon.description: One emoji, repeated once per unit, e.g. "🧍".

total.description: How many icons to draw: the whole. 100 makes a 10×10 grid.

count.description: How many of them light up: the part.

heading.description: What is being compared, e.g. "Earth next to Jupiter, by volume".

value.description: The number, in the unit the slide names.

items.description: Circles whose areas are proportional to the values. Smallest to largest reads best.

heading.description: What the scale measures, e.g. "How loud is loud? (decibels)".

marks.description: Points on the scale, each between min and max.

format.description: "year" shows 1963 rather than 1,963. Assumed for unit-less whole numbers between 1000 and 2100.

ends.description: Words at the low and high ends, e.g. ["Acid", "Alkaline"].

colors.description: Bar colours at the low and high ends.

heading.description: The process, e.g. "How a vaccine trains the immune system".

cycle.description: The last step leads back to the first.

heading.description: The instruction, e.g. "Match the scientist to the discovery".

pairs.description: Correct pairs; the app shuffles the right-hand side.

explanation.description: Shown once every pair is matched.

heading.description: The question each item answers, e.g. "Fact or myth?" or "Mammal or not?".

bin.description: 0 for the first bin, 1 for the second.

clue.description: The hint, e.g. "The process plants use to turn light into sugar".

answer.description: The word, shown as shuffled letter tiles.
Index of the odd one out, counting from 0.

explanation.description: Why it doesn’t belong, and what the others share.

heading.description: What to rank, e.g. "Which emits the most CO₂ per person?"

value.description: The number, in the unit the slide names.

items.description: Any order; the app shuffles them and the reader taps from largest to smallest. Values must all differ.

heading.description: The measure, e.g. "Known moons" or "Boiling point".

value.description: The number, in the unit the slide names.

items.description: In play order: the first is shown, then the reader guesses higher or lower for each of the rest.

question.description: e.g. "Out of 10 adults, how many don’t get enough exercise?"

total.description: How many icons: 10 or 20 are easiest to count.

answer.description: How many really count: the real share, rounded.

question.description: e.g. "How loud is a rock concert?"

step.description: Slider step; defaults to a hundredth of the range.

answer.description: The real value, between min and max.

format.description: "year" shows 1963 rather than 1,963. Assumed for unit-less whole numbers between 1000 and 2100.

ends.description: Words at the low and high ends, e.g. ["Silence", "Pain"].

colors.description: Bar colours at the low and high ends.

hints.description: Known points shown on the scale as clues, e.g. a whisper at 30 dB.

src.description: File name of an MP4 clip in content/media/<post-id>/. Make it with `npm run clip`.

poster.description: A still from the clip, shown before it plays (`npm run clip` makes one).

alt.description: What the clip shows, for screen readers.

fit.description: "contain" shows the whole frame on the field colours (default, best for landscape footage); "cover" fills the slide.

animation.description: true for an animated explainer drawn for this post (`npm run explainer`) rather than footage. Explore lists these under "Animation".

credit.description: Who made the footage and its licence, e.g. "NASA/JPL-Caltech · Public domain · excerpt".

href.description: The page the footage comes from, e.g. its NASA or Wikimedia Commons page.

music.description: Credit for the soundtrack, required when the clip has audio, e.g. "“Mesmerizing Galaxy” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0".

steps.description: The clip's steps in order, in seconds: when each caption or stage appears and when it goes. The player marks them on the seek bar, jumps between them and can pause at the end of each. The clip needs a keyframe 0.3 s before each step ends (where a paused clip shows it), one within 1 s before each start, and keyframes at most 4 s apart; `npm run explainer` writes the steps and encodes the clip that way.

complexity.description: How much a viewer must know and keep in mind to follow it, 1–10.

shock.description: Shock factor: how far the result is from what most people expect beforehand, 1–10.

ratings.description: The short's ratings, shown with it in the app. Score them with the scales in "Rating a short" in content/README.md.

source.description: Where a reader can check the claim. Prefer Wikipedia or a primary/academic source.

theme.description: Override the field colours. Pick dark enough colours for white text.

author.description: Who wrote it. LLM contributors use kind "ai".
